ch5-e1.caption: Phase portrait of $\dot x = -y + \lambda x(x^2+y^2),\ \dot y = x + \lambda y(x^2+y^2)$ for $\lambda < 0$: counter-clockwise inward spirals into the origin even though the linearisation predicts a centre.
ch5-e1.title: Linearisation failure at a centre (lambda < 0)

ch5-e10.caption: Phase portrait of $\dot x = y,\ \dot y = -\sin x - k y|y|$ ($k = 0.5$): energy decay $\dot E = -k|y|^3$ forces orbits to wind inward toward $(0,0)$ despite the linearised centre.
ch5-e10.title: Exercise 10: Quadratically damped pendulum

ch5-e2-i.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(0,0)$ is an unstable node, $(0,1)$ is a saddle, and $(2,0)$ attracts all interior trajectories (competitive exclusion of $y$).
ch5-e2-i.title: Exercise 2(i): Competitive exclusion

ch5-e2-ii.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(0,0)$ is an unstable node, $(2,0)$ and $(0,1)$ are saddles, and $(8/7, 6/7)$ is a globally attracting stable node in the first quadrant.
ch5-e2-ii.title: Exercise 2(ii): Stable coexistence

ch5-e2-iii.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(4/7, 2/7)$ is a saddle whose stable manifold separates trajectories tending to $(2,0)$ from those tending to $(0,1)$.
ch5-e2-iii.title: Exercise 2(iii): Bistable competition

ch5-e2-iv.caption: Nullclines and closed periodic orbits encircling the centre $(2/3, 1/2)$ in $x, y > 0$; $(0,0)$ is a saddle.
ch5-e2-iv.title: Exercise 2(iv): Lotka-Volterra predator-prey

ch5-e2-v.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: trajectories spiral inward toward the coexistence equilibrium $(2, 1)$ (stable spiral); $(0,0)$ and $(8,0)$ are saddles.
ch5-e2-v.title: Exercise 2(v): Predator-prey with logistic prey

ch5-e2-vi.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(0,0)$ is an unstable node, $(10,0)$ and $(0, 1/10)$ are saddles, and all interior trajectories approach $(97/13, 11/13)$.
ch5-e2-vi.title: Exercise 2(vi): Predator-prey with predator carrying capacity

ch5-e2-vii.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(0,0)$ and $(3,0)$ are saddles, and $(2,1)$ is a stable spiral attracting all interior orbits.
ch5-e2-vii.title: Exercise 2(vii): Predator-prey with logistic prey

ch5-e3-i.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: $(0,0)$ is an unstable node, $(1,0)$ and $(0, 1/2)$ are saddles, and all positive trajectories converge to the mutualistic coexistence node $(3, 2)$.
ch5-e3-i.title: Exercise 3(i): Bounded cooperative coexistence

ch5-e3-ii.caption: Nullclines and phase portrait for $x, y \ge 0$: the nullclines do not intersect in the positive quadrant, so positive trajectories grow without bound ($x, y \to \infty$).
ch5-e3-ii.title: Exercise 3(ii): Unbounded mutualism

ch5-e4-i.caption: Quadratic potential $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}\omega^2 x^2$ (top) and its elliptical closed orbits around the centre $(0,0)$ (bottom, drawn for $\omega = 1$).
ch5-e4-i.title: Exercise 4(i): Harmonic oscillator potential and phase portrait

ch5-e4-ii.caption: Double-well potential $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^4 - x^2$ (top) and phase portrait (bottom): centres at $(\pm 1, 0)$, saddle at $(0,0)$, and the figure-eight homoclinic separatrix $E = 0$.
ch5-e4-ii.title: Exercise 4(ii): Double-well potential and phase portrait

ch5-e4-iii-robinson.caption: Robinson potential $V(x) = \frac{1}{6}x^6 - \frac{5}{4}x^4 + 2x^2$ (top) and triple-well phase portrait (bottom): centres at $0, \pm 2$ and saddles at $\pm 1$ with separatrices.
ch5-e4-iii-robinson.title: Exercise 4(iii): Robinson triple-well potential and phase portrait

ch5-e4-iii-sheet.caption: Potential as printed in the sheet, $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^6 - \frac{5}{4}x^4 + 2x^2$ (top), which has a single minimum at $x=0$, yielding closed orbits around $(0,0)$ (bottom).
ch5-e4-iii-sheet.title: Exercise 4(iii): Printed sextic potential and phase portrait

ch5-e5-i.caption: Conservative motion on the wire $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2$ ($\omega = 1$, $g = 1$): closed periodic orbits encircling the centre $(0,0)$.
ch5-e5-i.title: Exercise 5(i): Parabolic wire phase portrait

ch5-e5-ii.caption: Conservative motion on the wire $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^4 - x^2$ ($g = 1$): centres at $(\pm 1, 0)$, saddle at $(0,0)$, and figure-eight separatrix $E = 0$.
ch5-e5-ii.title: Exercise 5(ii): Double-well wire phase portrait

ch5-e6-i.caption: Damped motion in $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2$ with damping $-\dot x$: all trajectories spiral inward to $(0,0)$.
ch5-e6-i.title: Exercise 6(i): Damped harmonic oscillator

ch5-e6-ii.caption: Damped motion in $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^4 - x^2$: the stable manifold of the saddle $(0,0)$ partitions the phase plane into the basins of the two stable spirals $(\pm 1, 0)$.
ch5-e6-ii.title: Exercise 6(ii): Damped double-well oscillator

ch5-e6-iii-robinson.caption: Damped motion in Robinson potential $V(x) = \frac{1}{6}x^6 - \frac{5}{4}x^4 + 2x^2$: trajectories settle into one of the three stable spirals at $0$ and $\pm 2$, separated by the stable manifolds of $\pm 1$.
ch5-e6-iii-robinson.title: Exercise 6(iii): Damped Robinson triple-well potential

ch5-e6-iii-sheet.caption: Damped motion in the printed sheet potential $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^6 - \frac{5}{4}x^4 + 2x^2$: every trajectory decays to the unique stable spiral $(0,0)$.
ch5-e6-iii-sheet.title: Exercise 6(iii): Damped printed sextic potential

ch5-e8.caption: Phase portrait of $\dot\theta = y,\ \dot y = -\sin\theta$: centres at $(2k\pi, 0)$, saddles at $((2k+1)\pi, 0)$, the $E = 1$ separatrix, bounded librations ($E < 1$), and unbounded rotations ($E > 1$).
ch5-e8.title: Exercise 8: Undamped simple pendulum

ch5-e9-over.caption: Phase portrait of the damped pendulum with $k = 2.5$: trajectories approach $(2m\pi, 0)$ as stable nodes without oscillation around the bottom.
ch5-e9-over.title: Exercise 9: Overdamped pendulum (k > 2)

ch5-e9-under.caption: Phase portrait of the damped pendulum with $k = 0.6$: trajectories spiral into the stable equilibria $(2m\pi, 0)$ while $((2m+1)\pi, 0)$ remain saddles.
ch5-e9-under.title: Exercise 9: Underdamped pendulum (0 < k < 2)

ch6-e1-iv.caption: Positive roots $\mu_n = \sqrt{\lambda_n}$ of $\tan\mu = -\mu/h$ (drawn for $h = 1$), with one root $\mu_n \in ((n - \frac{1}{2})\pi, n\pi)$ in each branch.
ch6-e1-iv.title: Exercise 1(iv): Graphical Robin eigenvalues

ch6-e8-i.caption: Periodic extension of $f(x) = x^2$ (continuous everywhere with corners at $x = \pm L$) compared with partial sums $S_1$ and $S_5$.
ch6-e8-i.title: Exercise 8(i): Fourier series of x squared on [-L, L]

ch6-e8-ii.caption: Periodic extension of $f(x) = e^x$ ($L = 1$) with jumps at $x = \pm L$: partial sums $S_2$ and $S_{10}$ converge to the midpoint $\cosh L$ at the discontinuities.
ch6-e8-ii.title: Exercise 8(ii): Fourier series of e^x on [-L, L]

ch6-e8-iii.caption: Periodic extension of $f(x) = 1$ ($x < 0$), $x+1$ ($x \ge 0$) ($L = 1$): continuous corner at $x=0$ and jumps at $x = \pm L$ converging to $1 + L/2 = 1.5$.
ch6-e8-iii.title: Exercise 8(iii): Fourier series of piecewise linear function
